money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Central African CFA Franc (XAF). Declare all amounts of local or foreign currency more than XAF200,000 on arrival and departure. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You can only cash traveller's cheques at larger banks in major cities. The cheques must be in either euros or US dollars. Gabon is largely a cash-based economy. Credit cards aren't widely accepted, except at major hotels and restaurants. Ask your bank if your cards will work in Gabon. You'll find ATMs in major centres. laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and can include long prison sentences in local jails. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Ensure you carry your identification and evidence of the purpose of your visit at all times. Local security forces may interpret laws broadly and inconsistently. You could break the law without intending to. The Australian Government can’t intervene in local judicial processes. It's illegal to photograph: airports the Presidential Palace government buildings military sites border posts It's illegal to buy or sell endangered wildlife products without a licence. This includes ivory and rhino horn. Local laws may change without notice.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships aren't legally recognised. Local communities can be intolerant towards same-sex relationships, so avoid public displays of affection. There have been attempts to charge people in same-sex marriages under public order and obscenity laws. - Advice for LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: Many pharmaceutical products are in short supply in Gabon. If you plan to bring medication, check if it's legal in Gabon. Take enough legal medication for your trip.
laws.heading: Medication

laws.rule: To drive in Gabon, you need both: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP) You must obtain your IDP before leaving Australia.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Smartraveller says to get a visa: people entering under visa-free arrangements have had immigration problems during their stay. A letter of invitation or sponsorship in French is also needed. Gabon has no mission in Australia; the nearest embassy is in Tokyo.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa before travel from a Gabonese mission (nearest in Tokyo); Gabon also runs an e-Visa site, but its content didn't load when read.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Arrange the visa, get a French-language invitation or sponsorship letter from the accommodation or sponsor (purpose, length of stay, the author's contact details), and carry a yellow fever certificate.

steps.step: Get a visa before travel rather than relying on visa-free entry.
Get a letter of invitation or sponsorship in French from the accommodation or sponsoring partner, stating the purpose and length of stay, and show it to immigration on arrival.
Check the Gabon e-Visa site, or contact the embassy in Tokyo, for the application.
Carry a yellow fever vaccination certificate.

documents: Invitation or sponsorship letter in French
